title: World Shaper — Upgrade Options
summary: Hearthhull, the Worldseed drains each opponent for 2 whenever you sacrifice a land, and once stationed it trades lands for cards. The stock list ramps far more than it needs to, is top-heavy, and has no way to protect its key pieces. Budget: up to €30 per deck in total (Cardmarket prices).

notes: Hearthhull's drain ('whenever you sacrifice a land, each opponent loses 2 life') is part of its 8+ station box, so it only works once Hearthhull has 8 charge counters. You station it by tapping creatures, adding counters equal to their power, so the deck needs creatures with high power (Juri, Uurg, Centaur Vinecrasher, Ob Nixilis, Moraug).
Top-heavy: 15 nonland cards cost 5 or more (World Breaker 7, Omnath 7, three 6-drops, nine 5-drops).
Too much ramp: 42 lands plus ~15 ramp pieces. Some ramp spells can become engines.
No protection at all for the commander or the board.
Interaction is good: ~10 spot removal, 6 at instant speed, 4 board wipes.
Mana base: Wastes is a colourless basic in a three-colour deck and should go.

Commander check: the card search flags that Hearthhull has no 'can be your commander' text (it's an artifact, not a creature). It is the precon's face commander, so check with your playgroup. Szarel, Genesis Shepherd (already in the deck) can legally be your commander.

Engine ledger — enablers: Zuran Orb (free), Hearthhull's own 2+ ability and Lotus Field sacrifice lands; Ramunap Excavator and Conduit of Worlds replay them from the graveyard; payoffs: Sabotender, Tannuk, Retreat to Hagra and Ob Nixilis drain on every land that enters, and Hearthhull's 8+ clause adds two more per sacrifice. Support: Tamiyo's Safekeeping and Snakeskin Veil protect the pieces, Countryside Crusher fills the graveyard with lands to replay. This is the most coherent of the three decks — every card references another.

Timing note: the drain only starts once Hearthhull is stationed to eight charge counters, which is a turn five-plus payoff. Before that the plan is the 2+ ability (sacrifice a land, draw two, play an extra land), so the early game is card advantage rather than damage.

Win conditions (finishers in the 99, counted by the deck-comparison skill's rule): big threats — Baloth Prime, Multani, Yavimaya's Avatar, Korvold, Fae-Cursed King, God-Eternal Bontu, Soul of Windgrace, Uurg, Spawn of Turg, World Breaker, Formless Genesis; armies and extra combats — Rampaging Baloths, Omnath, Locus of Rage, Titania, Protector of Argoth, Moraug, Fury of Akoum, Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest, Scouring Swarm; drain and burn — Mayhem Devil, Braids, Arisen Nightmare, Worldsoul's Rage.

core.name: Core package
core.description: Cheap protection (Tamiyo's Safekeeping covers Hearthhull before it's a creature; Snakeskin Veil covers creatures), plus a free outlet that turns any land into a 2-life drain once Hearthhull is at 8+. It also removes the colourless Wastes. Planetary Annihilation stays: with Hearthhull at 8+ and Mayhem Devil out, a mass land sacrifice is a finisher.

swaps.why: One mana: hexproof and indestructible on any permanent you control, including Hearthhull before it becomes a creature. Satyr Wayfinder is a weak 2-drop that only digs for a land.
One mana: hexproof and a +1/+1 counter on a creature you control, which makes a targeted removal spell fizzle. Escape to the Wilds is a 5-mana card-draw spell; Tannuk and Hearthhull cover card draw.

0 mana: sacrifice a land and gain 2 life. With Hearthhull at 8+ each opponent also loses 2, so any spare land becomes a drain, at instant speed and for no mana. With Sylvan Safekeeper it is one of the two free sacrifice outlets the deck is built on. Wastes was the only colourless basic in a three-colour deck.

directions.name: Scorched Earth Drain
directions.pitch: Sacrifice lands every turn and replay them from the graveyard. Sabotender, Tannuk, Ob Nixilis and Valakut Exploration deal damage on every land that enters from turn 2; once Hearthhull is stationed to 8, each land you sacrifice also costs every opponent 2 life, so Genesis Device, Nahiri's Lithoforming and Planetary Annihilation end games. Juri, Countryside Crusher, Ob Nixilis and Baloth Prime grow or make bodies with every land played or sacrificed, so they station Hearthhull quickly. It struggles when Hearthhull is removed twice or your graveyard is exiled; then Avenger of Zendikar, Omnath and Rampaging Baloths have to win in combat.
directions.plays_like: Burns the table out with land sacrifices

swaps.why: Play lands from your graveyard, so a land you sacrifice comes back with your next land drop and can be sacrificed again; with Azusa that is up to three a turn. Arcane Signet was a mana rock that did nothing for the land plan, and the deck has plenty of other ramp.
Another way to play lands from your graveyard, and its tap ability lets you cast a nonland permanent card from there (sorcery speed, as your only spell that turn). Cultivate is redundant ramp.
Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1, from turn 2 on, before Hearthhull is stationed. Night's Whisper is generic draw; Hearthhull's own 2+ ability draws two cards per land.

Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1, and the second trigger each turn draws a card. With Hearthhull's extra land play and lands replayed from the graveyard, that happens most turns. Groundskeeper's 'return a basic land' is redundant now that Ramunap, Conduit and Szarel let you play lands straight from the graveyard.
Each land that enters drains each opponent 1, or gives a creature deathtouch. Eumidian Wastewaker only works when it attacks, and its effect is symmetrical.

Gets a +1/+1 counter every time a land goes to your graveyard (every Zuran Orb, Hearthhull or fetch-land sacrifice), so it grows fast and stations Hearthhull. Each upkeep it mills lands off your library, which Ramunap, Conduit and Szarel let you play. Gaze of Granite also destroys your own cheap permanents (Zuran Orb, Juri, Sabotender); Blasphemous Act stays as the creature wipe.
Every land that enters can make a player lose 3 life and puts three +1/+1 counters on Ob Nixilis, which makes it one of the best creatures for stationing Hearthhull. World Breaker costs 7.

Land swap. When it enters you sacrifice two lands: with Hearthhull at 8+ that's 4 drain to each opponent, plus Juri counters, Mayhem Devil pings and two lands for Ramunap to replay. Then it taps for three mana of one colour. Viridescent Bog can't make mana on its own ({1},{T} only).

Land swap. Play it, then pay {1}, tap and sacrifice it for a basic Swamp, Mountain or Forest: a sacrifice trigger between two landfalls (the second makes Tannuk draw), and the replay engines bring it back to do it again.

how_to_play.summary: Station Hearthhull to 8 with Zuran Orb or Sylvan Safekeeper on the table: every land you sacrifice then costs each opponent 2 life, and one Genesis Device, Nahiri's Lithoforming or Planetary Annihilation turn finishes the table. Sabotender, Tannuk, Ob Nixilis and Valakut Exploration hit on every land that enters and Mayhem Devil on every sacrifice; Avenger of Zendikar, Rampaging Baloths, Omnath and Moraug win in combat if Hearthhull is answered.

sections.title: How Hearthhull works
points: Station (sorcery speed): tap another creature you control to put charge counters equal to its power on Hearthhull. A creature that came in this turn can do it.
2+: {1}, tap, sacrifice a land: draw 2 and you may play an extra land this turn. This is your card draw engine.
8+: it becomes a 6/7 creature with flying, vigilance and haste, and every land you sacrifice makes each opponent lose 2 life. Before 8 counters Hearthhull drains nothing.

sections.title: Turns 1–4: set up
points: Ramp: Sol Ring, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Harrow (sacrifices a land, then two untapped basics), Skyshroud Claim (two untapped Forests = two landfalls), Tireless Provisioner (a Treasure or Food per land).
Get a landfall payoff down: Sabotender, Tannuk or Valakut Exploration. They deal damage before Hearthhull is stationed.

Get a free outlet (Zuran Orb, Sylvan Safekeeper) and a replay engine early: Ramunap Excavator, Conduit of Worlds or Szarel let you play lands from the graveyard, and Undergrowth Recon returns one every upkeep. Without them, sacrificed lands wait for Splendid Reclamation, Aftermath Analyst or Worldsoul's Rage.

sections.title: Turns 4–7: build the engine
points: Cast Hearthhull and station it with high-power creatures: Juri (grows on every sacrifice), Countryside Crusher (grows when lands hit your graveyard), Ob Nixilis (three counters per landfall), Baloth Prime (10/10; each land you sacrifice makes a tapped 4/4 Beast and removes one of its six stun counters), The Gitrog Monster, Formless Genesis tokens, Titania's 5/3s and the tokens from Rampaging Baloths and Omnath.
Szarel puts counters equal to its power on another creature each time you sacrifice a nontoken permanent on your turn: put them on the creature you station with.

Every turn: sacrifice lands with Zuran Orb or Sylvan Safekeeper (both free), Hearthhull's 2+ ability, Evendo Brushrazer (tap: {R}{R}) or a fetch land, then replay one from the graveyard. Azusa adds two land plays a turn, so with a replay engine you can replay three lands a turn.

sections.title: Big turns and finishers
points: Genesis Device ({3}{G}{G}, tap and sacrifice it), Nahiri's Lithoforming, Planar Engineering and God-Eternal Bontu sacrifice several lands at once. With Hearthhull at 8+ each one is 2 life from each opponent; Juri and Korvold grow on each (Korvold also draws), Mazirek puts a counter on each of your creatures, Mayhem Devil pings, Titania makes a 5/3 and Baloth Prime a 4/4.

Worldsoul's Rage, Splendid Reclamation, Aftermath Analyst, Genesis Device and Planar Engineering put many lands onto the battlefield at once: Tannuk, Sabotender, Valakut Exploration, Ob Nixilis (3 life from one player each), Avenger of Zendikar's Plants, Rampaging Baloths and Omnath all trigger.
Moraug: every land that enters in your main phase gives an extra combat, and your creatures untap for it.

Planetary Annihilation with Hearthhull at 8+: you keep six lands and every land you sacrifice drains 2, Mayhem Devil pings for every land any player sacrifices, Hearthhull (toughness 7) survives the 6 damage, and Titania's tokens are created after the damage, so they survive. Juri dies to it unless it already has six +1/+1 counters, and then deals its power to any target.

sections.title: Tips
points: Zuran Orb and Sylvan Safekeeper cost nothing and work at instant speed: sacrifice in response to land destruction, or on an opponent's turn when the drain finishes someone. Undergrowth Recon brings a land back on your upkeep.

Lotus Field sacrifices two lands when it enters; play it when Hearthhull is at 8+ or a replay engine is out. Crop Rotation ({G}, instant) can fetch it, Ramunap Ruins, or Bojuka Bog to exile a graveyard in response.

Ramunap Excavator, Conduit of Worlds and Szarel let you play lands from the graveyard, not extra lands. Extra land plays come from Azusa (two), Hearthhull, Exploration Broodship (at 3+ counters), Oracle of Mul Daya, The Gitrog Monster and Nahiri's Lithoforming.

Nahiri's Lithoforming makes your lands enter tapped for the rest of the turn. Horizon Explorer makes the lands from Genesis Device, Planar Engineering, Splendid Reclamation and Undergrowth Recon enter untapped.

Stationing taps your creatures, and they stay tapped until your next untap step, so they can't block. Hold Tamiyo's Safekeeping or Defend the Rider for Hearthhull: they protect it even before it is a creature, which Snakeskin Veil and Sylvan Safekeeper can't.
At 8+, attack with Hearthhull first (vigilance keeps it untapped), then use its draw ability after combat.
Mulligan hands with fewer than 3 lands or with no ramp and no sacrifice outlet.

directions.name: Landfall Army
directions.pitch: Turn the deck's extra land drops into creature tokens, mana and damage. Hearthhull's extra land plays and the sacrifice-and-replay loop trigger landfall several times a turn.
directions.plays_like: Wide board of tokens; explosive turns

swaps.why: Every land that enters makes a Treasure or a Food. Ramp that keeps paying off, unlike a one-shot sorcery.
Play an extra land each turn, and return lands to your hand to replay them for more landfall.
Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1.
Every land that enters drains a player for 3 and grows Ob Nixilis.
A 1/1 Saproling on every landfall; with extra land drops and replays, that's several tokens a turn.
Makes a Plant per basic land when it enters, and every landfall puts four +1/+1 counters on a Plant.
A same-cost 7-drop that wins games: a 0/1 Plant per land you control, and every landfall grows them all. It also fuels Phylath.

how_to_play.summary: Turn every land drop into tokens, mana and damage, and win with a wide board.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Early: Tireless Provisioner (Treasure or Food per land), Tunneling Geopede (ping per land), Mina and Denn (extra land play each turn).
Mid: Ob Nixilis (3 drain per land), Sporemound (Saproling per land), Phylath (a Plant per basic you control, then four counters on a Plant per landfall).
Late: Avenger of Zendikar: a Plant per land you control, then every landfall grows all of them. Rampaging Baloths and Omnath add 4/4s and 5/5s.

sections.title: Tips
points: Mina and Denn can return a land to your hand to replay it: an extra landfall each turn.
Fetch lands and self-sacrificing lands (Evolving Wilds, the Courtyard cycle) are two landfalls each.
This version cuts Juri, so station Hearthhull with Ob Nixilis, Avenger's Plants and Baloth tokens.

directions.name: Lands Recursion
directions.pitch: Treat your graveyard as a second hand of lands. Loop Life from the Loam, replay lands with Crucible effects, and draw cards off discarded lands. This direction grinds out the longest games.
directions.plays_like: Grindy value; never runs out of cards

swaps.why: Return three lands from your graveyard to your hand, and dredge it back instead of drawing to keep the loop going. Endless fuel for Hearthhull.
Play lands from your graveyard, and recast a permanent from there each turn.
2 mana: your lands have hexproof, and for {2} you return a land from your graveyard to your hand. Moraug is a 6-drop.
Returns two lands from your graveyard to your hand when it enters, for more sacrifice fuel.
Makes a Plant whenever lands hit your graveyard (each Hearthhull activation), and can return a land by sacrificing three creatures.
Grows on landfall; discard a creature to put a land from your graveyard onto the battlefield.
Mills lands off the top every upkeep (Loam fuel) and grows whenever a land hits your graveyard. A 3-drop instead of a 7-drop.

how_to_play.summary: Treat your graveyard as a second hand of lands and grind long games with card advantage.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Life from the Loam returns three lands from your graveyard to your hand, and dredge brings it back instead of drawing.
Conduit of Worlds and Szarel let you play lands from the graveyard; Marwyn ({2}) and Tilling Treefolk return lands to your hand.
Turntimber Sower makes a Plant whenever lands go to your graveyard, which happens on every Hearthhull activation.

sections.title: Tips
points: Countryside Crusher mills lands off your library each upkeep (fuel) and grows; Floral Evoker puts lands from the graveyard onto the battlefield.
Hearthhull's 2+ ability (sacrifice a land: draw 2) is the engine; Loam keeps the lands coming back.
Watch for graveyard hate; spread your threats between graveyard and battlefield.

directions.win_conditions_note: Trades Moraug, Bontu, Rampaging Baloths and World Breaker for land recursion; it still wins through Hearthhull's drain, Braids, Mayhem Devil and 13 finishers, well above the 5–8 target.

recommendation: Scorched Earth Drain uses Hearthhull best: the landfall pingers deal damage from turn 2, and once Hearthhull is stationed to 8 every sacrifice and replay is another 2-point drain. All three directions stay under €20 including the core package.

bracket3.name: Bracket 3 package
bracket3.rule: Bracket 3 (Upgraded) allows up to three Game Changers, no mass land denial, no chained extra turns, and game-ending two-card combos only late in the game.
bracket3.description: The deck already drains hard. What bracket 3 asks for is speed and consistency, so this package adds a second free sacrifice outlet, more land drops and mana, a tutor for your best land, cheaper removal and three cards that sacrifice several lands in one go and bring new ones in.
notes: Planetary Annihilation: bracket 3 does not allow mass land denial. The card leaves every player six lands, so most tables accept it, but ask yours. Toxic Deluge (about €4) is the replacement if they don't.

How it wins faster: with Hearthhull at 8+ charge counters, Sylvan Safekeeper or Zuran Orb turns every land into 2 life from each opponent for no mana. Genesis Device and Planar Engineering sacrifice several lands in one card and fetch new ones; Nahiri's Lithoforming draws a card for each land and lets you play that many more. Avenger of Zendikar turns the landfall from those turns into an army.
Changed on 2026-11-15: Genesis Device replaced Lotus Cobra in the package, and Scapeshift (about €31) is no longer a premium option because Genesis Device does the same thing.

swaps.why: Game Changer. One green mana at instant speed: sacrifice a land (a Hearthhull trigger) and put any land from your library onto the battlefield, such as Lotus Field (two more sacrifices), Ramunap Ruins or Bojuka Bog, or Field of the Dead if you add it. Centaur Vinecrasher is a trampler that enters with a counter per land card in all graveyards and returns to hand for {G}{G}, but it doesn't sacrifice or replay lands; 12% of Hearthhull decks keep it.

A second Zuran Orb on a one-mana creature: sacrifice a land for free, at any time, as often as you like, and the target creature gains shroud. In 61% of Hearthhull decks. Loamcrafter Faun (17%) returns a few cards once.

Three mana: it enters and puts a basic land onto the battlefield tapped. Later, for {3}{G}{G} at sorcery speed, you tap and sacrifice it, sacrifice any number of lands and fetch that many lands. With Hearthhull at 8+ counters and eight lands, that is 16 life from each opponent before the landfall triggers. It is Scapeshift's effect for about a tenth of the price. Sprouting Goblin's sacrifice ability costs {R} and a tap for one card.

Two extra land drops on each of your turns. With Ramunap Excavator, Conduit of Worlds or Szarel you replay the lands you sacrificed: each one is another landfall, and each can be sacrificed again for another drain. This copy came from Landing Party on 2026-11-16, which got Ka-Zar of the Savage Land instead.

A Treasure or Food for every land that enters: real ramp in a deck that puts three or four lands onto the battlefield in a turn. Hammer of Purphoros costs {2}{R} and a land for one 3/3, and Hearthhull already has haste at 8+ counters.

Every land that enters exiles the top card of your library and lets you play it. Cards you don't play become damage to each opponent at your end step. Pest Infestation only hits artifacts and enchantments, at two mana per target.

Two mana at instant speed destroys any permanent an opponent controls (they may fetch a basic land). Binding the Old Gods costs four at sorcery speed and only hits nonland permanents, though it also fetches a Forest a turn later.

Sacrifice X lands, draw X cards and play X extra lands this turn (they enter tapped). With Hearthhull at 8+ counters that is 2X life from each opponent, and Ramunap Excavator or Conduit of Worlds lets you replay the same lands. Tireless Tracker's Clues draw one card for two mana each.

Sacrifice two lands and put four basic lands onto the battlefield tapped: two sacrifice triggers and four landfall triggers from one card. Ob Nixilis alone takes 12 life with it. Uurg's sacrifice costs {B}{G} a land where Zuran Orb and Sylvan Safekeeper are free, and its power counts the land cards in your graveyard, which the replay engines keep emptying.

A 0/1 Plant for every land you control, and every land after that puts a +1/+1 counter on each Plant: an army that grows with each land drop. Multani is one large creature: removal answers it until you pay {1}{G} and return two lands to your hand to get it back, and exile answers it for good.

premium.why: Game Changer. The deck plays 28 differently named lands, so once seven are out, every land that enters also makes a 2/2 Zombie, including lands you replay from the graveyard. Crop Rotation fetches it. It replaces one of the eight Forests.

Game Changer. It untaps everything you control on each opponent's turn, so Hearthhull's ability (sacrifice a land: draw two cards) works four times a round instead of once, and at 8+ counters every use drains the table.

deck_changes.why: Returns a land from your graveyard to the battlefield every upkeep without using a land drop, so a land sacrificed on an opponent's turn comes back, triggers landfall and can be sacrificed again. Twilight Mire only fixed mana.
One mana, instant: hexproof and indestructible for Hearthhull while it is still a noncreature artifact. Rakdos Charm's modes were narrow, and Bojuka Bog takes over the graveyard hate.
A red source that can pay {2}{R}{R} and sacrifice itself for 2 damage to each opponent, plus Hearthhull's drain at 8+. Ramunap Excavator, Szarel or Conduit of Worlds replay it every turn.
Back from the loose pile. It gets a +1/+1 counter for every permanent you sacrifice, and station counts power, so Juri charges Hearthhull. Retreat to Hagra was the weakest of ten landfall payoffs.
Back from the loose pile. The land recursion replays it, so it exiles an opponent's graveyard again and again.
